title: Supplementary Fig. 1 | Pairwise network distances in the main simulation
notes: Frobenius distances over the same 1,800 candidate TF-TG pairs, divided by each run's maximum pairwise distance and averaged over 3 datasets x 5 model seeds (ground truth: one sequence per dataset). Titles: temporal smoothness (Fig. 2f). max_distance: unnormalized maximum pairwise distance, mean and SD across datasets.

title: Supplementary Fig. 2 | Benchmark on a random (non-modular) network
notes: One random-network dataset (data seed 101), model seeds 0-2 (Random: independent uniform scores). a, b: candidate AUROC per stage, mean and SD across model seeds. c: mean temporal smoothness, mean and SD across model seeds.

blocks.subtitle: c: temporal smoothness (and overall candidate AUROC)

title: Supplementary Fig. 3 | Sensitivity to prior size, temporal change and inactive candidates
notes: Settings: a, candidate TFs per TG (12, 16, 20); b, % active edges replaced between adjacent stages (5, 10, 12); c, % candidates inactive per stage (50, 62.5, 70). Three datasets x 3 model seeds; points = mean of dataset means, error bars = SD across datasets. Panel a was drawn from the 4-decimal cluster summary; the individual fits below reproduce it within rounding. Ground-truth smoothness is 0.5 in all settings.

title: Supplementary Fig. 4 | GRN inference on a branching simulated lineage
notes: a: RNA t-SNE coordinates of dataset 101 (1,600 cells). b: AUROC per stage (T0, T1 shared; A2-A4 and B2-B4 branches), mean over three datasets of the mean over three model seeds; SD across datasets. c: temporal smoothness over the seven parent-child pairs, same aggregation; ground truth from the generating GRN.

title: Supplementary Fig. 5 | Top TFs of the 12 mouse edge clusters
notes: Up to 12 TFs with the highest out-degree per edge cluster: degree = distinct target genes within the EC, aggregated across cell clusters (bar length); mean_score = mean inferred edge score (bar colour). panel_title: cell clusters with the highest representation of the EC (fraction of unique edges).

title: Supplementary Fig. 6 | GO enrichment of the ten mouse LDA topics
notes: GO Biological Process 2021, background 7,764 network target genes; one-sided hypergeometric test, BH-adjusted within each topic. Ten highest-ranked terms per topic; score = -log10(adjusted P) (bar length).

title: Supplementary Fig. 7 | Temporal smoothness of baseline TF-TG networks
notes: Pairwise Frobenius distances between stage TF-TG networks, divided by the largest distance, for SCENIC+ (published stage eRegulons), scDoRI (official v1.0.0 path scores) and random networks; germline (15 stages) and soma (9 time points). Smoothness = 1 - mean adjacent distance / largest distance; for the soma along each branch.

title: Supplementary Fig. 8 | Top 10 TFs by centrality in each germline edge cluster
notes: For each edge cluster (frozen numbering EC0-EC11), the ten TFs (243-TF list) with the most distinct target genes in the cluster (degree, bar length) and their mean edge score (bar colour). Panel titles from the stage composition of each cluster.

title: Supplementary Fig. 9 | GO enrichment of the 12 germline LDA topics
notes: Enrichr with FlyEnrichr GO_Biological_Process_2018 on the target genes of each topic's 500 highest-weighted edges; the ten terms with the highest score = -log10(adjusted P) per topic (adjusted P = 0 shown as 300). Panel titles from the topic weights per stage (Fig. 4f).

title: Supplementary Fig. 10 | Mondo temporal profiles of DRAFT and its ablations (seed 2025)
notes: Plotted curves (each scaled to its maximum = 1) on the dense stage grid: centrality = sum of Mondo's selected outgoing TF-TG scores, Gaussian-smoothed (sigma = 0.5 stage) and interpolated; mean log-normalized expression; number of distinct SCENIC+ targets in the published stage eRegulons (DAR = yes, DEG = yes). Stage values before smoothing and scaling below.

title: Supplementary Fig. 11 | Controls for peak shifts between TF network activity and expression
notes: a: observed number of TFs with a peak shift (>= 3 stages) and 10,000 random re-pairings of network and expression profiles (box: median, quartiles, 2.5th-97.5th percentiles; full null distribution below). b: per seed pair, fraction of TFs shifted in the second seed among TFs shifted / not shifted in the first, with one-sided Fisher P. c: Spearman rho of network-peak stages between full DRAFT and models with a different seed (shuffled TF-RE prior, no GRU, Linear + GRU).

blocks.subtitle: c: model pairs, full DRAFT and shuffled prior

title: Supplementary Fig. 12 | Agreement of early/late calls between methods
notes: Percentage of candidate LR pairs (four directions pooled, 322 pairs) on which two methods make the same early/late call, counting pairs timed by both. DRAFT: mean over the five germline models (somatic receivers: one model). The plotted values were computed before SdA and SdB were treated as one parallel time point; 'current_value' and the per-model values below use the current alignment (differences < 0.6 percentage points). CellChat, LIANA+ and the LR expression product do not depend on the seed.

title: Supplementary Fig. 13 | Stability of DRAFT early/late calls across germline models
notes: Per direction and scope: pairs with the same call in 5, 4 or 3 of the five germline models (seeds 2024-2028), Fleiss' kappa and agreement between two models (mean and range over the ten model pairs). Random: expected proportions if each model placed each pair's peak on a uniformly random germline stage. The plotted values were computed before SdA and SdB were treated as one parallel time point; the last table repeats the analysis with the current alignment (only the soma-to-germline 'all candidates' row changes: 61/5/8, kappa 0.82).

title: Supplementary Fig. 14 | Soma-to-germline benchmark under different alignments
notes: AUROC of the earliness score for the 21 literature-supported soma-to-germline pairs versus other candidates (germline model seed 2025); found = literature pairs whose score peaks early. All methods use the same alignment and gates.
